Critical — P1 / Major Incident threshold reached

intel.application: Application incident. In ServiceNow, check if there is an existing Problem Record for this application — recurring application incidents often indicate an unresolved known error. Use the Agent Assist suggestions that appear when you enter the Short Description in ServiceNow.
intel.infrastructure:
Infrastructure incident. In ServiceNow, ensure the affected CI is linked accurately — the CMDB dependency map will show downstream services that may be impacted but not yet reporting issues. Check for any recent changes in the caused_by field.

ServiceNow CMDB impact ↗
intel.thirdparty:
Third-party/Supplier incident. In ServiceNow, populate the caused_by field with any relevant change and raise a Supplier Management record if this represents a service level failure. Consider whether your supplier SLA requires formal notification — many do within 2 hours for P1. Ensure your vendor escalation contact is in the escalation matrix.

Supplier incident handling ↗
intel.security:
Security incident detected. In ServiceNow, route to your Security Operations team, not standard IT Ops. Consider raising a Security Incident record (sn_si_incident table) separately from the standard incident. Engage your CISO or security lead immediately. In regulated environments, DORA (Article 17(3): defined escalation procedures; Article 19: reporting of major ICT-related incidents) and FCA SUP 15 may require rapid escalation and notification.

ServiceNow Security Operations ↗
intel.data:
Data/Database incident. If personal data may be affected, your Data Protection Officer must be notified within 72 hours under UK GDPR. In ServiceNow, flag the Privacy Impact field if available. Consider whether DORA operational incident reporting thresholds are met for financial services.

ICO breach reporting ↗
intel.network: Network incident. Network incidents often have multiple downstream application impacts not immediately visible. In ServiceNow, use the CMDB CI dependency view to identify affected services before closing. Consider whether monitoring needs tuning to catch similar issues earlier.
intel.process: Process/Human factor incident. The root cause involves a process or human element. In the RCA stage, focus the Fishbone analysis on the People and Process categories. In the problem record, consider whether a Knowledge Article or updated runbook would prevent recurrence — not a technical fix.

doraSource: Article 17 covers the ICT-related incident management process, Article 18 the classification of incidents and Article 19 the reporting of major ICT-related incidents.

Article 17(3) requires incident management processes to assign roles and responsibilities and to keep senior management and the management body informed of major incidents; it does not prescribe a human-review gate.
Article 9(4)(e) covers ICT change management and Article 9(4)(f) patch and update policies.
DORA (Article 17(3): defined escalation procedures; Article 19: reporting of major ICT-related incidents) and FCA SUP 15 may require rapid escalation and notification.
DORA Article 9(4)(f) requires financial entities to have appropriate and comprehensive documented policies for patches and updates.

dora_article_17.title: DORA Article 17 — ICT-related incident management process
dora_article_17.summary: Requires financial entities to define, establish and implement an ICT-related incident management process to detect, manage and notify ICT-related incidents (Art. 17(1)). All ICT-related incidents must be recorded, with procedures that ensure root causes are identified, documented and addressed (17(2)). The process must include early warning indicators, classification procedures, assigned roles and responsibilities, communication and internal escalation plans, and reporting of major incidents to senior management and the management body (17(3)).

dora_article_18.title: DORA Article 18 — Classification of ICT-related incidents
dora_article_18.summary: Establishes the criteria by which ICT-related incidents are classified as major. Classification determines whether Article 19 reporting obligations are triggered. The detailed classification criteria and materiality thresholds are set out in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 (published 25 June 2024). Thresholds shown in this tool are a simplified aid — verify against the Delegated Regulation.

dora_article_19.title: DORA Article 19 — Reporting of major ICT-related incidents
dora_article_19.summary: Financial entities must report major ICT-related incidents to their competent authority (Art. 19(1)) by submitting an initial notification, an intermediate report and a final report (Art. 19(4)). Article 19(4) leaves the time limits to the technical standards: under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301, Article 5, the initial notification is due within 4 hours of classifying the incident as major and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of it; the intermediate report within 72 hours of the initial notification; and the final report no later than one month after the intermediate report (or latest updated intermediate report). Reporting applies once an incident is classified as major under Article 18.
